name: mc-smoke
description: Monte Carlo harness acceptance test: diode-connected nfet_01v8 mismatch. Not a comparator circuit.
claim: None -- harness self-verification, not a spec claim. Proves the Monte Carlo plumbing (rndseed reproducibility, the tt_mm local-mismatch switch, and the deterministic negative control) actually takes effect on a real sky130 device, so later offset-sigma distribution records against this repo's own target-spec table (top-level README, DRAFT) can be trusted.

notes: Harness acceptance testbench (issue #8), ported from 2AMLogic/sky130-sar-adc's identical fixture (commit b80c144efbf467a586f728726cabb25c1eb5a1f2) -- same PDK, unchanged. The negative control (N draws at the plain 'tt' corner, mismatch disabled, same seed sequence as the 'real' tt_mm draws) must reproduce vgs_nfet EXACTLY (stdev == 0) -- see sim/harness/mc_runner.py's negative_control_ok() docstring for why a nonzero negative-control stdev invalidates the accompanying distribution.

The positive control requires the mismatch-ENABLED (tt_mm) draws' vgs_nfet stdev to exceed the min_stdev floor above -- 1e-6 V, comfortably below the mismatch-driven spread observed empirically in sky130-sar-adc's own port source and reconfirmed in this repo's own bootstrap run (issue #8; see sim/mc-smoke/records/), but strictly above zero, so a regression that silences MC_MM_SWITCH (collapsing both arms to stdev == 0) is caught even if floating-point noise alone would technically satisfy a bare '> 0' check. See sim/harness/mc_runner.py's positive_control_ok() docstring.
